solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Marvellous epicurean perhaps could be heard

indicators.note: what is heard is what reaches the ear, so the spoken sound of the words counts, not their spelling

parts.note: an epicurean is one kind of diner, and could be is might; said together without an R they run into one word

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a marvellous gourmet could be heard at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent DINER MIGHT and DYNAMITE sound the same. 'Perhaps' flags epicurean as just one example of a diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamite is informal praise for something terrific or sensational, a slang synonym for excellent.

clue.text: I'd advise you to assess trouble in joint

parts.note: the emphatic imperative, as in 'do come', is a way of urging someone
to vet is to check or assess
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A doctor advises a patient to have a sore joint looked at.
explanation.walkthrough: DO + VET + AIL. 'Joint' suggests a body part, but here it is woodworking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is an interlocking woodworking joint made of fan-shaped tenons fitted into matching mortises.

clue.text: Some number in edges on equilaterals, squares

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for number
taken as written

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost ends, so only its first and last letters are wanted

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson about counting the sides of equilateral triangles and squares.
explanation.walkthrough: N + IN + ES. The geometry words are only there for their letters; 'squares' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three times three, so nines are perfect square numbers, examples of the class named.

clue.text: Old president works on a way to take charge to a greater extent

parts.note: a mill is a works or factory
taken as written
RD, short for road, is a way
to take a charge or load is to fill up
more means to a greater degree

explanation.surface: A former president's works pave the way for him to take even more charge.
explanation.walkthrough: MILL + A + RD + FILL + MORE. 'Take charge' reads as assuming command, but it means taking on a load.
explanation.definitionFit: Millard Fillmore was the thirteenth President of the United States, serving from 1850 to 1853.

clue.text: Piece of cake kennelling stray dog

indicators.note: to kennel is to house an animal inside a shelter, so one part shelters another

parts.note: a tier is one layer of a wedding cake
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A stray dog is given shelter in exchange for a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: T(ERR)IER. 'Piece of cake' suggests something easy, but it means a layer of a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed type of small, lively dog originally used for hunting burrowing animals.

clue.text: One counted on a god seeing sacrifice of Church

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to sacrifice something is to give it up, so letters are surrendered from the word

parts.note: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A believer relies on a god who demands that the Church make sacrifices.
explanation.walkthrough: A + BAC(CH)US with CH removed. 'One counted on' sounds like a trusted person, but it is literally a device people count on.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads that people use for arithmetic, so calculations are literally done on it.

clue.text: Second rate shot blunted at first in each and every game

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit within it, so one group goes inside another
at first points to the start of a word, so its opening letter alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
every one means all
taken as written
a volley is a shot struck before the ball bounces
B grade is second rate, after A

explanation.surface: A disappointing, blunted shot spoils every single game a player tries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second rate' looks like a judgment but supplies only a grade letter, and 'each and every' is split so the shot can sit in the gap between its two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Beach volleyball is an Olympic sport played by pairs on sand, so it is one kind of game.

clue.text: Drink: last few bars stocking a lot

indicators.note: a shop stocking goods holds them within it, so one part is kept inside another

parts.note: a coda is the closing passage of a piece of music
reams means a great quantity, especially of writing

explanation.surface: At closing time the last few pubs have a lot of drink in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: C(REAMS)ODA. 'Bars' suggests pubs, but these are bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet, vanilla-flavoured carbonated soft drink.

clue.text: Drop prominent display

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small amount of liquid added, as of milk
second meaning: a showy, eye-catching feature, as in making a big news story

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it sounds like taking down a display; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a small dash of liquid, and also a conspicuous showing, as in a front-page feature or making a big impression.

clue.text: Denouement unresolved, page missing

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a pending matter is not yet settled
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A novel's climax is left unresolved because its final page has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: PENDING without its P. The surface suggests a torn-out book, which fits the definition well.
explanation.definitionFit: A denouement is the final resolution of a plot, so it is the close or conclusion of a story.

clue.text: Mercenary backing Channel 5

indicators.note: going backwards means moving the wrong way, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: a lane is a channel or route, as in a shipping lane
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A greedy investor is putting money into a TV station, Channel 5.
explanation.walkthrough: LANE + V, read backwards. 'Channel 5' is a British TV station, so it reads as one name, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone who acts only for money and can be bribed, so they are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Play a note and strike a chord?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally sound one note on a bell
second meaning: seem familiar, jog the memory

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves sound musical, so the second looks literal too; in fact it is the idiom for something seeming familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for prompting a sense of recognition, and the first is also a literal musical action.

clue.text: Maestro returned books with study in India

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
to scan is to examine closely
taken as written
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A conductor brings back library books after a period of study in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned books' looks like a trip to the library, but OT is the Old Testament, and India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian conductor, and maestro is the title for a distinguished conductor.

clue.text: Drone linked to superpower remains on the ground

parts.note: a drone is a low continuous hum
the United States is a superpower

explanation.surface: A military drone tied to a superpower stays grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM + US. 'Drone' suggests an aircraft and 'remains on the ground' sounds like it won't fly, but the definition is a noun for decayed matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Humus is the dark organic soil material formed from decayed plant and animal remains lying in the earth.

clue.text: Mole inhabiting drains I'd eradicated

indicators.note: to inhabit is to live inside a place, so the answer lives within the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second word, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A garden mole living in the drains has been wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: draINS I'D ERadicated. The surface suggests the burrowing animal; the definition is the spy sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy or informant planted within an organisation, which is someone working on the inside.

clue.text: Eccentric snooker player might do this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crazy, oddball person
second meaning, read as two words: put backspin on the cue ball

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an adjective describing the player, but it is a separate definition. In snooker, to screw the ball is to hit it low so it spins back after contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwball is informal for a crazy person, and in two words it names a snooker shot played with backspin.

clue.text: Pass with badge sent over for huge cardinal

parts.note: to go is to pass or move along

indicators.note: something sent over is flipped back across, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: a logo is an emblem or badge

explanation.surface: A huge cardinal of the Church is handed a pass and a badge.
explanation.walkthrough: GO + LOGO backwards. 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but here it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: A googol is ten to the power one hundred, an enormous whole number, which is what a cardinal number is.

clue.text: Lady unclothed has broken more than one bike chain belonging to the Greeks

indicators.note: to break into something is to split it open and get inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: bikes are cycles

indicators.note: stripping off clothes removes the outer layer, so only the inner letters stay

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters stripped away

explanation.surface: A naked woman has wrecked several Greek bicycles and a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: CYCL(AD)ES. 'Chain' looks like part of a bike, but it is a chain of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades are a group of Greek islands in the Aegean Sea, and a group of islands is called a chain.

clue.text: Bothersome judicial work

definitions.note: a noun phrase, where the answer is the verbal noun of try
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what a judge does when hearing a case in court

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one phrase describing tedious legal work, but they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying means irritating or testing your patience, and judges try cases, so hearing them in court is their job.

clue.text: British composer like Brahms or Wagner, say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Edward, an English composer of light opera
second meaning: of the nationality those two composers share

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a British composer in the style of two famous Germans, but Edward German (1862-1936) was an English composer, known for the comic opera Merrie England.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of an English composer is also the nationality adjective that fits Brahms and Wagner, both born in Germany.

clue.text: Charlie has put away a black jumper

indicators.note: putting something away stores it inside, so one piece is tucked within another

parts.note: in British slang a charlie and a wally are both a fool
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Charlie has packed away his black sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: WALL(AB)Y. A jumper is a British sweater, which is the obvious reading, but here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaby is a small kangaroo-like marsupial that moves by hopping, so it is a jumper in the literal sense.

clue.text: Case of wife forbidding picture

indicators.note: a case is the outer covering, so only the letters at the two ends are wanted

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
forbidding and stern both mean severe and unfriendly

explanation.surface: A husband's wife forbids him to buy a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: WE + STERN. 'Forbidding' reads as a verb but is the adjective meaning grim, and 'picture' means a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a film about cowboys in the American West, and picture is an old word for a film.

clue.text: Burn with rage about king

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: steam is anger, as in letting off steam
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A furious king smoulders with anger.
explanation.walkthrough: ST(R)EAM. 'Burn' looks like a verb about anger; it is the Scottish noun for a small river.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England a burn is a small river or brook, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Eight, it's inferred, carrying old cloth

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds another
something inferred is only implied, so a number must be worked out from part of another number's spelling

parts.note: two thirds of twelve is eight, so the first two thirds of its letters stand for it
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone deduces that eight people are carrying some old cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: A puzzle within the clue: eight is two thirds of twelve, so the first four of TWELVE's six letters stand for it. T(O)WEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is a piece of absorbent cloth used for drying, so the definition names its material.

clue.text: One needing to be driven home after ancient-looking cocktail

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another in the reading order

parts.note: something rusty looks old and neglected

parts.words: One needing to be driven home
parts.note: a nail is hammered in until it is driven home

explanation.surface: A drinker who must be taken home after an old-fashioned cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One needing to be driven home' sounds like someone too drunk to drive, but it is a nail being hammered in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusty nail is a cocktail made of Scotch whisky and Drambuie, a named mixed drink.

clue.text: Greek framework extremely lacking

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so lacking them leaves just the inside

parts.note: a lattice is a framework of crossed strips, here without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Greek structure that is badly short of something.
explanation.walkthrough: (L)ATTIC(E). 'Greek' looks like a person, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means relating to Attica or ancient Athens, so it is a regional synonym for Greek.

clue.text: Dry talk on flag recalled

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the second-named piece is placed first
something recalled is called back, so it runs the other way

parts.note: to flag a path is to pave it with flagstones
to orate is to talk at length

explanation.surface: A dull lecture about flags is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: PAVE backwards + ORATE. 'Dry talk' reads as a boring lecture, but Dry is a verb on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to turn liquid into vapour, which leaves a surface dry, so both verbs mean drying out.

clue.text: Did something one day — about time!

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
T is the abbreviation for time
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone finally took action one day, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: AC(T)E + D. 'About time!' sounds like an exasperated cheer, but it puts the time letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to take action or do something, so the past tense matches the phrase.

clue.text: A fishy style?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a haircut, short at the front and long at the back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy style' reads like a dodgy fashion; the question mark warns that a fish and a haircut share the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an edible sea fish and a famously unfashionable hairstyle, short on top and long behind.

clue.text: Pin loose, fasteners here and there

indicators.note: something loose is not held in order, so its letters can fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
laces fasten shoes

explanation.surface: A pin has come loose and the fasteners are scattered about.
explanation.walkthrough: PIN rearranged + LACES. The comma makes 'Pin loose' look like a broken fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: In places means at scattered points or in some spots, which is the sense of here and there.
